records.title: Labeled matrix display
records.caption: The native calculator displays a 2x2 working matrix with labeled rows and columns.

records.title: Symmetric matrix check
records.caption: The two off-diagonal entries match, so the pairwise symmetry check succeeds.
records.focus:
--- Original A ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  2.000000  1.000000  |
  Row  2 |  1.000000  3.000000  |


  --- Transpose A^T ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  2.000000  1.000000  |
  Row  2 |  1.000000  3.000000  |


  Result: A is SYMMETRIC (A = A^T).

records.title: Asymmetric matrix check
records.caption: The original input is compared with its transpose and correctly classified as asymmetric.
records.focus:
--- Original A ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  4.000000  7.000000  |
  Row  2 |  2.000000  6.000000  |


  --- Transpose A^T ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  4.000000  2.000000  |
  Row  2 |  7.000000  6.000000  |


  Result: A is NOT symmetric.

records.title: Identity matrix check
records.caption: A 3x3 identity input passes the diagonal and off-diagonal checks.
records.focus:
--- Matrix A ---

  Matrix (3 x 3):
            Column 1  Column 2  Column 3
  Row  1 |  1.000000  0.000000  0.000000  |
  Row  2 |  0.000000  1.000000  0.000000  |
  Row  3 |  0.000000  0.000000  1.000000  |


  Result: A IS an identity matrix.

records.title: 2x2 determinant
records.caption: Gaussian elimination returns determinant 10 for the bundled 2x2 example.

records.title: 3x3 determinant
records.caption: The classic 3x3 example has determinant 1, providing a known-value calculation.

records.title: Singular inverse rejection
records.caption: Dependent rows are detected, and the calculator reports that an inverse does not exist.
records.focus:
--- Matrix A ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  1.000000  2.000000  |
  Row  2 |  2.000000  4.000000  |

  Determinant = 0.00000000

  Sorry: inverse does not exist for this matrix
  (determinant is zero).

records.title: Unique linear-system solution
records.caption: For A x = [18,14], elimination returns the known solution x = [1,2].

records.title: Matrix multiplication
records.caption: A = [[4,7],[2,6]] times B = [[1,2],[3,4]] produces [[25,36],[20,28]] via the native triple-loop product.

records.title: Scalar multiplication
records.caption: A negative scalar multiplies every cell without replacing the working matrix.
records.focus:
Enter the number k: 
  --- k * A ---

  Matrix (2 x 2):
             Column 1   Column 2
  Row  1 |  -8.000000 -14.000000  |
  Row  2 |  -4.000000 -12.000000  |

records.title: Matrix trace
records.caption: The trace is the sum of the two diagonal entries, 4 + 6.

records.title: Rank of dependent rows
records.caption: Row reduction finds one independent row in this 3x3 matrix.
records.focus: Rank(A) = 1

records.title: 3x3 adjugate
records.caption: The direct cofactor implementation transposes the cofactor matrix to form the adjugate.

records.title: Singular 4x4 adjugate
records.caption: The larger singular case has a valid adjugate with bottom-right value 6.

records.title: 3×3 inverse verification
records.caption: The calculator inverts a 3×3 upper-triangular matrix (determinant 8), then multiplies A by that inverse entered as B. The product is the identity, confirming A × A⁻¹ = I.

records.title: Zero first pivot
records.caption: Partial pivoting swaps rows and preserves the determinant sign.
records.focus:

            Column 1  Column 2
  Row  1 |  0.000000  2.000000  |
  Row  2 |  3.000000  4.000000  |


  Determinant = -6.00000000
